You said

Can a Asustor DRIVESTOR 4 Pro (AS3304T) NAS that has the following specs run self-hosted app Immich on Docker?:

• Realtek RTD1296 1.4GHz Quad-Core 64-bit CPU

• 2 GB DDR4

Gemini said

Technically, yes, you can run Immich on an Asustor AS3304T via Docker, but it will be a "stripped-down" experience. Your hardware specs are significantly below the official requirements, so you will need to make major adjustments to prevent the NAS from crashing or freezing.

The Hardware Reality Check

ComponentAS3304T SpecImmich RequirementVerdict
RAM2 GB DDR4 (Non-upgradable)4 GB (Min) / 6 GB+ (Rec)Severe bottleneck.
CPURTD1296 (ARM64)2-4 CoresSupported, but slow for indexing.

Why 2 GB RAM is problematic

Immich is a heavy application suite composed of several microservices (PostgreSQL, Redis, the Server, Microservices, and Machine Learning).

  • PostgreSQL: Usually requires around 256 MB – 512 MB just to run reliably for a large library.

  • Machine Learning (ML): This is the "dealbreaker." The ML container alone often spikes to 1 GB+ during facial recognition or smart search indexing. On a 2 GB system, this will trigger the Linux "OOM Killer," which will shut down your containers or the entire NAS OS to save itself.

How to make it work (The "Low-RAM" Strategy)

If you decide to proceed, you must follow these steps to keep the system stable:

  1. Disable Machine Learning: In your docker-compose.yml, do not start the immich-machine-learning container. Without this, you lose facial recognition and "smart search" (searching for "dog" or "beach"), but the core photo backup and viewing will function.

  2. Limit Docker Resources: Use Docker Compose "deploy" limits to prevent any one service from eating all the RAM.

    services:
  immich-server:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 500M

  3. Turn off "Media Mode": Asustor has a "Media Mode" in ADM settings that reserves 512 MB of RAM for its own multimedia apps. Disable this to give that RAM back to Docker.

  4. Slow and Steady Import: Don't dump 50,000 photos at once. The RTD1296 CPU will struggle with thumbnail generation. Upload in small batches or use the immich-go CLI tool to upload from a computer, which offloads some processing.

Performance Expectation

  • Web/App Speed: Loading the timeline will be snappy enough once thumbnails are generated.

  • Background Tasks: Thumbnail generation and video transcoding will be slow. A large video might take several minutes to process.

  • Stability: If you run other heavy apps (like Plex) simultaneously, you will likely run into memory errors.

Recommendations

If you find Immich too heavy, consider PhotoPrism (also heavy but slightly more tunable) or stick with the built-in ASUSTOR Photos, which is specifically optimized for your NAS's Realtek chip and 2 GB RAM.
